facts.text: Mill Bay sits at the northeast tip of Kodiak Island, surrounding the small bay that gives the community its name.
The Alutiiq people have lived on Kodiak Island for over 7,500 years, with archaeological sites near Mill Bay.
The Alutiiq Museum and Archaeological Repository in Mill Bay showcase indigenous heritage alongside Russian colonial history from the late 18th century.
Mill Bay’s climate is subpolar oceanic (Köppen Cfc), with cool summers, mild winters, and average temperatures moderated by North Pacific currents.
The area receives about 78 inches of precipitation each year, mostly rain, with winter snowfall around 70 inches, creating a wet, foggy environment.
Glacial history carved U‑shaped valleys and fjord‑like inlets around Mill Bay, leaving steep rocky shores and gravel/sand deposits near stream outlets.
